notes.meaning: Paul still considers the believers in Corinth his brothers in the faith, but their spiritual growth has stalled. Instead of being guided by the Holy Spirit, they are acting like worldly people who follow their own selfish desires. They are like spiritual infants who are just taking their first steps.

Just as a tiny baby can drink only milk, the Corinthians could only receive the simplest, most basic truths about Jesus. Paul had to feed them with easy lessons when he first arrived because they were not ready for deeper teaching. Sadly, even after all this time, their ongoing immaturity means they still cannot handle solid food.

The clear proof of their worldly attitude is the jealousy and fighting breaking out in their church. When Christians argue, take sides, and try to outdo one another, they are acting just like people who do not know God. True spiritual life produces love and peace rather than bitter rivalry.

The Corinthians were splitting into rival factions based on their favorite Christian speakers. Paul even rebukes those who claim him as their special leader, showing that he refuses to have a personal fan club. By acting like passionate fans of human teachers, they were behaving just like the ungodly culture around them.

Preachers and leaders are not party bosses or founders of rival groups. They are simply humble servants whom the Lord used to help people believe the good news. Each minister performs only the specific task that God assigned to them.

Paul compares the church to a farm where different workers do different chores. Paul arrived first and planted the gospel seed by starting the church, and Apollos followed to water it with further teaching. Yet neither human worker could create life; only God caused the spiritual seed to take root and grow.

Compared to God, the human workers are nothing on their own. They are useful tools in His hands, but they have no power to forgive sins or change human hearts. Because of this, all the credit and praise for church growth belong entirely to God.

The different teachers are not competitors, because they share one single purpose in serving Christ. Even though they work together as one team, God holds each servant personally responsible for their work. When the Lord evaluates them, He will reward each one based on their faithful effort, not their worldly popularity.

Gospel ministers work together under God's guidance and for His glory. The church members do not belong to any preacher, because they are God's own cultivated field. Paul also introduces a second picture, reminding the believers that they are God's building.

By God's grace, which gave him the calling and the skill, Paul acted like an expert builder by laying the foundation of the church in Corinth. Other teachers were now building the rest of the structure on top of that base. Paul warns every teacher to be extremely careful about what they teach and how they build.

There is only one true foundation that can support the church, and that is Jesus Christ Himself. No church can safely rest on human traditions, philosophy, or personal leaders. Anyone trying to build on any other base is setting up something that will ultimately collapse.

Builders use different kinds of materials as they add to the foundation of Christ. Gold, silver, and costly stones represent pure, durable, and sound biblical truths that honor God. Wood, hay, and straw stand for cheap, flimsy human opinions and worthless traditions that cannot last.

A coming day of judgment will bring the truth about every teacher's work out into the open. The Lord will test each person's work with fire, revealing what kind of materials they used. God's fiery inspection will show whether a ministry was made of solid truth or worthless rubbish.

If a Christian leader taught the truth faithfully, their work will survive the testing fire of judgment day. That faithful servant will receive a special reward from the Lord for their labor. This shows that careful and honest service to God will never be forgotten.

If a teacher spent their life building with useless, fleshly ideas, all that work will be burned away, and they will suffer the loss of their reward. Yet because their personal faith rested on Christ the foundation, they themselves will still be saved from eternal condemnation. They will escape just like someone rushing out of a burning house with only their life.

Paul reminds the Corinthian Christians that together as a local church, they form God's holy temple. In the Old Testament, God dwelt in a stone temple, but now the Holy Spirit makes His home among His gathered people. Remembering this sacred truth should inspire believers to live with great reverence and love.

Because God's spiritual temple is holy and precious to Him, anyone who harms or tears it down faces severe judgment. A person can destroy a church by spreading false doctrine, encouraging sin, or stirring up bitter divisions. God takes the protection of His people seriously and will bring ruin on those who corrupt His church.

People easily fool themselves when they rely on human intellect and worldly prestige. If anyone wants to be truly wise in God's eyes, they must let go of their pride and be willing to look like a fool to this world. Embracing the simple truth of the gospel requires humble submission rather than worldly arrogance.

The cleverest wisdom of this world is complete foolishness in the presence of the all-knowing God. Paul quotes from the book of Job to show that God catches crafty thinkers in their own clever traps. Human schemes can never outsmart God's perfect plan.

Paul provides another scriptural proof by quoting from the Psalms. The Lord searches the hearts of men and knows that the proud reasoning of worldly minds is empty, useless, and temporary. Human thinking without God cannot lead anyone to eternal life.

Because human wisdom is empty and teachers are only servants, believers must stop boasting about following particular men. Christians already have an abundant inheritance through Christ, so they do not need to limit themselves to one human leader. God has given all things to work together for the good of His people.

Instead of believers belonging to preachers, all faithful teachers—such as Paul, Apollos, and Peter—are given by God to serve the church. Even the world, life, physical death, the present time, and the future belong to God's children. Nothing in this life or the next can defeat believers, because God directs everything for their eternal benefit.

Believers do not belong to human teachers, because they have been purchased by Jesus Christ and belong entirely to Him. Christ Himself honors and serves God the Father as the mediator between God and humanity. This brings everything to a wonderful conclusion, uniting all believers under the loving rule of God.
